passages.body:

passages.title: Family Bookstore Celebrates 50 Years
passages.body:
SPRINGDALE — Hollis & Daughters Books will celebrate its 50th anniversary this Saturday with readings, live music, and free cake for visitors. The store was opened in 1975 by Walter Hollis and is now run by his daughters, Ruth and Ellen.

Like many independent bookstores, Hollis & Daughters struggled when online shopping became popular. “About ten years ago, we nearly closed,” said Ruth Hollis. The sisters turned things around by adding a café, hosting book clubs, and inviting local authors for monthly events. Sales have grown every year since 2017.

Saturday's festivities begin at 10 A.M. Local author Daniel Price will read from his new novel at 2 P.M.

passages.title: City Bike Share — Frequently Asked Questions
passages.body:
How do I rent a bike?
Download the CityRide app, scan the QR code on any bike, and you're ready to go.

How much does it cost?
Single rides cost $1 to unlock plus $0.20 per minute. A monthly membership ($20) includes unlimited rides of up to 45 minutes each.

What if I ride for more than 45 minutes?
Members pay $0.20 per additional minute.

Where can I return a bike?
At any of our 150 stations. Bikes left outside a station will be charged a $25 fee.

Are helmets provided?
No, but riders under 18 are required by law to wear one.

passages.title: ★★★★☆ Harborline Ferry Tours — “Great views, crowded deck” — posted by J. Akande
passages.body:
My husband and I took the two-hour sunset tour last Saturday. The guide was knowledgeable and funny, and the views of the coastline were breathtaking. We even saw a family of dolphins near the lighthouse!

My only complaint is that the boat was very crowded. It was hard to find a spot on the upper deck to take photos. If you go, I recommend booking a weekday tour, when there are fewer passengers, or arriving early to board first.

The tour includes a drink, and snacks are available for purchase. At $45 per person, I think it's good value.

passages.title: Airport Unveils Expanded Terminal
passages.body:
WESTON (September 12) — Weston International Airport opened its new east terminal on Monday after three years of construction. [[1]] The $480 million expansion adds 14 gates, a larger security checkpoint, and more than 30 shops and restaurants.

Airport director Helen Quist said the project was necessary to keep up with rising passenger numbers. Traffic at the airport has grown by 40 percent over the past decade. [[2]]

Travelers will also notice several new features designed to reduce waiting times, including self-service bag drop machines and a mobile app that shows security wait times in real time. [[3]]

Not everyone is pleased, however. Some residents of nearby neighborhoods have complained about increased noise from additional flights. [[4]] Ms. Quist said the airport is working with the city to study noise-reduction measures.

passages.title: Four-Day Workweek Trial Shows Promising Results
passages.body:
A six-month trial involving 45 companies in the region has found that a four-day workweek can maintain productivity while improving employee well-being. Under the program, employees worked 32 hours per week for the same pay.

According to the final report, published yesterday by the Workplace Research Institute, 38 of the 45 companies plan to continue the arrangement. Participating businesses reported fewer sick days and a 15 percent drop in staff turnover. Revenue remained stable on average.

“The results exceeded our expectations,” said lead researcher Dr. Marcus Lindahl. He cautioned, however, that the trial was voluntary. “Companies that signed up were likely already open to flexible work, so we should be careful about generalizing these findings.”

Not all participants were convinced. Several manufacturing firms said the schedule created gaps in production coverage, and two customer service centers returned to a five-day week after customers complained about longer waiting times.

Dear Volunteers,

Thank you for all your hard work this year. Thanks to you, more than 600 animals found new homes. [[1]]

Starting next month, weekend shifts will be divided into two parts, 8 A.M. to 12 P.M. and 12 P.M. to 4 P.M., instead of a single eight-hour shift. [[2]] Many of you told us that the long shifts were tiring, and we hope this change will allow more people to volunteer.

Please use the online calendar to sign up for shifts. [[3]] If you have already signed up for a full-day shift in November, you will automatically be assigned to the morning shift. [[4]]

Thank you again for your dedication.

Rachel Kim

questions.trap: « automatically » : aucune nouvelle inscription n'est nécessaire.

questions.prompt: In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3], and [4] does the following sentence best belong? “If you would prefer the afternoon instead, simply change your booking in the calendar.”
questions.explanation: « instead » s'oppose à l'affectation automatique au créneau du matin, mentionnée juste avant [4].
questions.trap: En [3], le créneau du matin n'a pas encore été évoqué : « instead » n'aurait pas de point de comparaison.
